newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Red Cross body sends envoy over Georgia deaths.
newsitem.headline: Red Cross body sends envoy over Georgia deaths.

text.p: The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) said on Tuesday it was working to maintain good relations with Georgia in the wake of a fatal accident involving its top official there.

A statement from the Geneva-based body also said the IFRC was sending a special representative to Tbilisi to facilitate direct contacts with the authorities in the ex-Soviet republic on issues relating to the incident.

Earlier on Tuesday, Georgian officials said they had asked for the diplomatic immunity of the IFRC Tbilisi delegation chief, 65-year-old Alexander Marinov, to be lifted to ease investigation of the accident.

Tbilisi Chief Prosecutor Nugzar Gabrichidze told Reuters two men were killed when a Red Cross vehicle driven by Marinov, former head of the International Department of the Bulgarian Red Cross, was involved in a collision early on Sunday.

The IFRC statement said its Secretary-General George Weber had written to the Georgian Foreign Ministry outlining "concrete steps" to make progress on issues surrounding the death of the two Georgians.
Weber's letter said the Red Cross body "would do its utmost to maintain good relations between Georgia and the Federation," the statement added.

Weber, a former national Red Cross chief in Canada, had decided to allow Marinov "to have an exchange of views" with the Georgian Interior Ministry and other ministries concerned about the circumstances of the accident, according to the statement.
It said the IFRC had appointed Anders Persson, a senior official of the Swedish Red Cross, as its special representative. A Federation spokesman said he would fly to Tbilisi shortly.
Foreign Minister Irakly Menagarishvili told reporters in Tbilisi that Georgia had asked the Federation to lift Marinov's immunity to "guarantee an objective investigation."

In Geneva earlier, IFRC spokesman Jon Valfells said the Federation was in close contact, and cooperating fully, with the Georgian authorities over the affair. "We want it investigated, just as they do," he added.

But he said no decision had yet been taken on the immunity request. Many heads of IFRC delegations -- the term the Federation uses for major offices around the world -- have diplomatic status by agreement with the national government.
Valfells said Weber had sent letters of condolence over the accident to Georgia's President Eduard Shevardnadze and to the relatives of the two who died.
The Federation, which specialises in disaster relief, is an umbrella body uniting national Red Cross and Red Crescent societies around the globe, including the Georgian Red Cross.
In Georgia, where thousands were killed and many more made refugees by civil conflicts after the collapse of the Soviet Union, it has four expatriate staff and several local employees.
